newsitem.title: UK: Graham Swift wins Britain's top literary prize.
newsitem.headline: Graham Swift wins Britain's top literary prize.

text.p: Favourite Graham Swift on Tuesday won Britain's Booker literary award for "Last Orders," his bizarre tale of four friends scattering at sea the ashes of a London butcher.
Swift, who beat off contenders from Canada, India and Northern Ireland, had been the hottest favourite in the 28-year history of Britain's prestigious prize.
Publisher Carmen Callil, head of the panel of judges for the 20,000 pound ($31,930) prize, said: "Choosing the winner was torture."
But she said of Swift's novel: "It is a book that we are sure will give pleasure to thousands of people."
The judges read 150 books by writers from 50 Commonwealth countries and Ireland before picking their shortlist of six.
The winner is sure of rocketing sales after all the pre-ceremony hype and appraisal by literary critics.
The six authors, used to the lonely profession of writing, confessed to being startled by the glare of media publicity that always surrounds the prize.
But they felt the unaccustomed publicity was worthwhile if their books reached a wider audience.

Northern Irish poet Seamus Deane, nominated for his first novel "Reading in the Dark," said: "It does feel a bit like a feeding frenzy and is a bit of a shock when you lead such a solitary existence."
Canadian writer Margaret Atwood, shortlisted for "Alias Grace," said of the prize: "It actively does encourage more reading but is hard on the authors, especially the younger ones.
"There is nothing you can do to win it. It's not like a horse race or the Olympics. Not having sex the night before won't help."

Beryl Bainbridge had to put up with being left on the Booker shortlist for the fourth time with her "Every Man for Himself." The other runners-up were Indian-born Rohinton Mistry, picked for "A Fine Balance," and Shena Mackay for "The Orchard on Fire."
Swift, 47, had been shortlisted for the Booker before for his novel "Waterland."
He took the Booker media glare in his stride, telling reporters: "It is a real honour to be on the short list. Literary awards don't encourage writers to write but they do encourage people to read."
